bib.title: Can Small Language Models Help Large Language Models Reason Better?: LM-Guided Chain-of-Thought

question: Can a small fine-tuned LM generate rationales that make a frozen black-box large LM answer multi-hop QA better than standard or CoT prompting?
hypothesis: Splitting CoT into rationale generation (small LM, trained by distillation then RL) and answer prediction (frozen large LM) improves answer accuracy and rationale quality.
contributions: LM-guided CoT framework: small LM generates rationale, frozen large LM predicts answer
Rationale distillation followed by RL with 8-aspect rationale-quality and task-accuracy rewards
Experiments on HotpotQA and 2WikiMultiHopQA with FLAN-T5

method.summary: FLAN-T5 small (80M) is instruction-tuned on filtered CoT rationales from a large LM, then refined with PPO using rationale-aspect rewards (classifier-based) plus a task reward from the frozen FLAN-T5 XXL (11B) answer prediction. At test time the small LM rationale is inserted into the large LM prompt.

datasets.name: HotpotQA
datasets.size: 15K random training samples (30K total with 2Wiki); eval 2000 instances
datasets.split: eval: 1000 instances ML answered correctly + 1000 answered incorrectly under standard prompting
datasets.preprocessing: only supporting paragraphs used as context due to FLAN-T5 input limit

datasets.name: Distillation set
datasets.source: rationales generated with CoT prompt, greedy decoding
datasets.preprocessing: filter responses with no rationale before final answer and with inaccurate answers

datasets.name: RL set
datasets.size: 5000 examples FLAN-T5 XXL failed to answer correctly

datasets.name: Human rationale annotation
datasets.split: correct n=78, incorrect n=22; classifier 90 train/10 eval

other.also: used as teacher? inferred: the distillation teacher is not named in the text (sentence is cut off in the PDF text); M^L is the likely source

other.note: footnote: zero-shot much worse than FLAN-T5; no numbers

training.objective: Stage 1: instruction-tuning (supervised) on rationales; Stage 2: PPO with reward R_aspect + R_taskAcc (R_taskAcc=1 if F1>0.5 else 0) and KL penalty to M^S

other.reward_classifiers: two logistic regression classifiers on TF-IDF (logic/coherence/consistency; fluency/naturalness/readability), trained on 90 labeled examples; factuality and relevance by token-level lexical overlap (Ye and Durrett 2022)
other.reward_aggregation: normalization or weighted summation tested, no effect on performance

inference.decoding: greedy for teacher rationale generation; SC baselines sample n=10 paths and take most consistent answer
inference.prompting: zero-shot; LM-guided prompt appends small-LM rationale r' then 'Hence, the answer is'

parameters.ranking_variant: sample multiple reasoning paths and rank by R_aspect; number of samples not stated

metrics.name: F1
metrics.definition: average word overlap between prediction and ground truth

metrics.name: Answer inclusion
metrics.definition: ground truth answer is mentioned in the prediction

eval.protocol: 2000 hard-filtered eval instances per dataset; single table, no seeds or significance tests reported; rationale quality validated with 3 annotators (mean Fleiss kappa 0.56)

limits: Only FLAN-T5 and only multi-hop QA tested; generalisation open (Sec 6).
Little human annotation due to resource constraints: reward classifiers trained on 100 labels, evaluated on 10.
Eval sets were hand-filtered to be hard (1000 correct + 1000 incorrect), so absolute numbers are not natural-distribution accuracy.
No seeds, variance or significance tests for Table 2; RL gains are tenths of a point.
Selecting top-quality rationales lowered task performance; authors do not explain.
XXL (11B) base shows CoT hurts, consistent with sub-50B models reasoning poorly; the black-box large LM here is not a >100B model.
